cells.tense: The strength you're leaning on right now is steady, and it's coming from you, not from the room.
cells.act: carry on with the version you chose through another week of doubt
cells.ask: Stay with the decision you made, without reopening it. Same direction, past the point where doubt usually pipes up. Nothing new to settle.
cells.core:
It holds. Whatever the load is this week — money, a tired body, a job that keeps asking — you're standing under it, and the strength is yours. Not borrowed, not granted. That's the shape when this is working: you bear the pressure and the pressure doesn't get to decide what you are.

Pick the decision you already made and stop re-arguing it. Not decide again. Stay with the version you chose, walking toward a light you picked before the sky turned. No sign has to justify it. If it turns out right you'll feel it as the week goes; if it turns out wrong, that's information too, and you'll get it faster than the re-arguing ever hands it over.

cells.tense: You're already bracing for the next thing to go wrong, and the bearing is happening before it's needed.
cells.act: return the favour at its true size
cells.ask: When someone does you a real turn — their time, a hand, a proper thank-you — give one back that same week, sized to match, and close it out.
cells.core:
You can bear what's on you. What's bending is that you're bearing it before it lands — the next bill, the next flare-up, the next thing that might break. Endurance turns into anticipation, and anticipation doesn't rest, so the strength stays running well before the load shows up, and no week is left with nothing being carried.

Try the other direction. When someone does you a real turn — their help, their time, a thank-you for what you held — give one back within the same week, sized to match theirs. Not a ledger, not favors owed and owing. One thing given, one thing returned, closed out, so the exchange isn't all on your side. What's coming is coming. Bearing it early doesn't make it lighter when it lands.

cells.tense: You've been under the load so long that you've stopped noticing you aren't moving anymore.
cells.act: do the giving in the open this time, where it was always done unseen
cells.ask: Choose a giving you'd normally keep quiet for someone — a chore, a repair, a small favor — and do it in a place where that person can watch you at it.
cells.core:
There was pressure, and you bore it, and then somewhere along the line you set down the reason you were doing it — the version of yourself that had plans, or the one that could want something. Your feet are still planted. Nobody's watching, so nobody knows. That's the shape when this has thinned: the bearing is real and the reason for it has slipped out of view.

Do a giving where it can be seen this week. Choose one you'd normally keep quiet — a chore, a repair, a small favor — and do it in a place where the person it's for can watch. Not announced, not explained. Just visible. The reason comes back that way — not by feeling it again, but by having someone else see that you have one.

cells.tense: You're already doing the standing, and somewhere along the line your name came off the record.
cells.act: keep following the star after everything that has happened
cells.ask: Put the direction you keep quietly going in on paper, with no plan attached, and continue in it unchanged. The line written is the only new thing.
cells.core:
You're bearing something that gets no audience — private, unglamorous, steady — and you've been filing it under circumstances rather than decisions. As if the strength appeared by chance and you happened to be nearby. You didn't; you've kept at it. That needs no proof for anyone else. It needs owning by you.

Put the direction on paper — the thing you keep going toward anyway, no plan attached — and keep going in it exactly as before. Nothing about the pressure changes. The difference is that it's yours now instead of something being done to you. Read the line again in a month; if it still holds, the record stands corrected. The bearing doesn't get lighter. It gets handed back to whoever was already standing under it.
